lessons: Give every row the same defense: at least 3 shooters plus a wall_nut in front; the weakest row is the one that breaks, so recount attackers per row every wave.
Build the economy first (4-5 sunflowers in cols 0-1, and replace any that die), then stop at wave 4-5 and spend everything on defense.
Rows 0 and 5 break early to single conehead leaks (wave 5-9); put 3 shooters and a wall_nut in them before wave 5, not a lone peashooter.
Rebuild every lost shooter, pad, sunflower, or wall_nut on the next turn, especially in a row whose mower is gone; a row with 0 attackers is already lost.
A fired mower is gone for good; once one fires, double that row's shooters and walls immediately and bomb the zombie clump.
Upgrade to repeaters/snow_peas by wave 8-10 in rows that have lost plants; plain peashooters can't kill buckethead (~70 peas) fast enough.
Place wall_nuts in cols 4-5 of every row early and replace any under 40%; zombies were reaching col 2-3 shooters because nothing stopped them.
Don't let sun sit near zero late: at wave 18 I had 25 sun and nothing affordable, so keep income up and bank 150+ for emergencies from wave 15.
Keep cherry_bomb ready for buckethead/conehead clumps before col 3 and use it on the row that is about to break, not on single zombies.
Replace damaged plants before the last waves instead of counting on them.
Don't let a lone zombie wander through a row with no shooters; put at least one fresh shooter plus a wall in that row right away.

history.summary: Won by stacking fume shrooms and potato mines in the middle columns, with mowers as backup, even though many forward puff shrooms were lost.
lessons: Night level with no falling sun: plant sun_shroom and sunflower early in the back columns (cols 1-2) before the first zombies arrive.
Fume_shroom in cols 3-4 of each row was the main killer; get one in every row that zombies use.
Potato_mines in cols 4-5 stopped coneheads and screen doors well; replant them as they are used.
Puff_shrooms are free but die quickly at col 5-6; use them as cheap filler, and don't expect them to hold the line.
Put wall_nut in front of the fume_shrooms (col 4-5) in the rows that get pressure, because fume range is short.
Row 1 had no mower and lost a sun_shroom there; keep that row's defense heavier.
Keep sun for replacing lost plants in the late waves (8-10), when pressure is highest.
Graves block planting at some tiles, so plan around them.

history.summary: I lost because coneheads, pole vaulters and screen doors in the final wave overran thin, low-damage defenses (mostly puff_shrooms and a few fume_shrooms) and the mowers were already used up, so row 3 broke through.
lessons: Night level with no falling sun: plant sun_shroom and sunflower early in cols 1-2 before the first zombies arrive. Keep building sun income until about wave 6.
Fume_shroom in cols 3-4 of each row was the main killer. Get one in every row and add a second in rows under pressure. Puff_shrooms alone can't kill coneheads.
Armored zombies (conehead, screen_door) beat puff_shrooms: 17 of them died. Don't rely on puffs for damage. Use them only as free fillers in front of fumes.
Waves 8-9 are the first real break (coneheads killed sun_shrooms and used mowers in rows 0, 1 and 3). Have a fume_shroom plus a wall_nut in every row by wave 7.
Potato_mines in cols 4-6 kill coneheads and screen doors. Replant them right after each one explodes, and stagger them so one is always armed in each row.
Put wall_nut at col 4-5 directly in front of the fume_shrooms. Replace it when damaged, since fume range is short.
Mowers were gone in rows 0-3 by wave 12, leaving no backup for the final wave. Don't let early leaks use them. Kill zombies before col 3.
Keep a sun reserve (150+) for wave 18-20, which is a huge flag wave with pole vaulters. I ended with only 45 sun and couldn't replace anything. Hold a cherry_bomb for the final wave.
Pole vaulters jump over the first plant, so a wall_nut doesn't stop them. Put a fume_shroom or potato_mine behind it.
Sun_shrooms in cols 1-2 were lost to leaks. Once the economy is established (about 8 producers), stop adding producers and spend on fume_shrooms.
Graves block planting at some tiles, so plan around them. Row 1 had no mower, so keep that row's defense heavier.

history.summary: Won by filling every row with 2-3 fume_shrooms backed by wall_nuts and a sun_shroom economy, plus constantly replanted potato_mines and a final cherry_bomb, which left 4 mowers unused.
lessons: Night level with no falling sun: plant sun_shroom and sunflower early in cols 1-2 before the first zombies arrive, and keep building income until about wave 6.
Fume_shrooms in cols 2-4 of every row are the main killers. Get at least 2-3 per row. Puff_shrooms alone can't kill coneheads, so use them only as free fillers.
Replant potato_mines in cols 4-7 right after each one explodes, and stagger them so one is always armed per row. They handled coneheads, screen doors and pole vaulters.
Put a wall_nut at cols 5-6 directly in front of the fume_shrooms, and replace it when damaged. Fume range is short.
Pole vaulters jump the first plant, so a wall_nut doesn't stop them. They killed fume_shrooms at col 4 in waves 13-19, so put a potato_mine or a second fume_shroom behind the nut.
Wave 5-9 leaks hit row 0 first (puff_shroom, sun_shroom, sunflower and the mower were lost). Put a fume_shroom plus a wall_nut in every row, row 0 included, by wave 5.
Once income is established (about 8 producers), stop adding producers and spend on fume_shrooms, nuts and mines.
Keep a sun reserve of 150+ for waves 18-20 and hold a cherry_bomb for the final flag wave. It worked: I finished with 125 sun and 4 mowers.
Replace dead fume_shrooms immediately in the final waves (3-4 died in wave 20). A mower is the last backup, so keep zombies from reaching col 1.
Graves block planting on some tiles, so plan around them. Row 0 had no mower after wave 6, so keep its defense heavier.

history.summary: Won by building a night economy early, then using fume_shrooms, nuts and mines to hold, with all five mowers used only on the final wave 8.
lessons: Night level with no falling sun: plant sun_shroom and sunflower early in cols 1-2 before the first zombies arrive, and keep building income until about wave 5-6.

Put a wall_nut at cols 5-6 directly in front of the fume_shrooms, and replace it when damaged. Fume range is short.

Put a fume_shroom plus a wall_nut in every row, row 0 included, by wave 5. Leaks often hit row 0 first.
Once income is established (about 8 producers), stop adding producers and spend on fume_shrooms, nuts and mines.
Keep a sun reserve of 150+ for the final waves and hold a cherry_bomb for the final flag wave.

Replace dead fume_shrooms immediately in the final waves. Mowers are the last backup, so keep zombies from reaching col 1. This level ended with 0 mowers even though I won, so build more defense before the last wave.
Graves block planting on some tiles (they are heavy in cols 3-6 on this map), so plan around them. Use grave_buster only if there is spare sun and you need the tile.
Check which rows have lost their mower, and keep those rows' defenses heavier.

history.summary: I lost because my defense was too thin: the fume_shrooms and puff_shrooms were all in cols 1-3 and got eaten by coneheads, there were no walls, and the mowers were spent by wave 10.
lessons: Night level with no falling sun: plant sun_shroom and sunflower early in cols 0-1 before the first zombies arrive. Keep building income until about wave 5, but don't over-invest, because this loss came from too little defense.

Fume_shrooms are the main killers. Get 2-3 per row, in cols 3-5 rather than cols 1-2, so zombies are hit long before they reach the producers. This loss had at most one fume per row and every row collapsed.
Puff_shrooms alone can't stop coneheads, and 8 of them died uselessly. Use them only as cheap fillers, never as the main defense.
Put a wall_nut in front of the fume_shrooms in every row, in cols 5-6, and replace it when it's damaged. Zombies chewing on the nut stay inside the fume range.
Replant potato_mines right after each one explodes, and stagger them so one is always armed per row (they take about 15 s to arm). Plant them ahead of the zombies, not at the last second.
Don't put producers (sun_shroom, sunflower) in cols 1-2 of a row that has no fume_shroom. A leak kills them and wrecks the economy. Rows that lose their mower need heavier defense.
Pole vaulters jump the first plant, so a wall_nut doesn't stop them. Put a potato_mine or a second fume_shroom behind the nut.
Keep a sun reserve of 150+ for the late waves, and use the cherry_bomb on a clump of coneheads before they reach cols 1-3. Don't hold it unused.
Replace dead fume_shrooms immediately. Mowers are the last backup, and once they are spent one leak ends the level.
Check every row, row 0 included, each wave. Leaks start in rows with zero attackers, so don't leave any row empty.
Graves block planting in cols 6-8 on this map. Plan around them, and use grave_buster only if there is spare sun.

history.summary: I lost because I relied on 14 puff_shrooms and only one or two fume_shrooms per row, so coneheads and footballs broke through every row and the mowers ran out by wave 10.

Put a wall_nut in front of the fume_shrooms in every row, in cols 5-6, and replace it when it's damaged. Zombies stuck on the nut stay inside the fume range.

Keep a sun reserve of 150+ for the late waves, and cherry_bomb a clump of coneheads or footballs before they reach col 3. I ended with 50 sun and an unused bomb, so don't hold it.
Check every row, row 0 included, each wave. Leaks start in rows with zero or one attacker, and once the mowers are spent one leak ends the level.
Graves block planting in cols 6-8 on this map. Plan around them, and use grave_buster only if there is spare sun.
Waves 8-10 bring many coneheads and footballs together. Have 2+ fume_shrooms plus a wall_nut in every row by wave 6.

history.summary: Won narrowly: fume_shrooms in cols 1-3 with potato_mines held most waves, but wave 10 broke through and all mowers were spent, leaving only a thin defense and 50 sun at the end.
history.plan:
Economy: Plant sun_shrooms first in cols 0-1, add a few sunflowers, and keep building income until about wave 5.
Defense: Put 2 fume_shrooms per row in cols 2-4. Put a wall_nut in cols 5-6 in front of them. Use puff_shroom as a cheap filler.
Zombies: Place a potato_mine in the football's row, and replant mines after they explode. Use cherry_bomb on a clump of coneheads or the football before col 3.
Reserve: Keep 150+ sun for later waves. Check all 5 rows every wave, and replace dead fume_shrooms and damaged wall_nuts immediately.
If a row breaks: Put a wall_nut and an extra fume_shroom there, or use cherry_bomb.
lessons: Night level with no falling sun: plant sun_shroom and sunflower early in cols 0-1 before the first zombies arrive. Keep building income until about wave 5, then switch to defense.
Fume_shrooms are the main killers. Get 2-3 per row in cols 2-4, and replace dead ones immediately. This level rows 0, 2 and 3 had only 0-1 fume_shrooms late, and wave 10 broke through them.
Puff_shrooms alone can't stop coneheads or footballs, and 7 died again. Plant only a few as cheap fillers, and spend the sun on fume_shrooms and wall_nuts.

Put a wall_nut in front of the fume_shrooms in every row, in cols 5-6, and replace it when damaged. Zombies stuck on the nut stay inside fume range. The board at the end showed no wall_nuts in the front rows, so I under-built here.
Replant potato_mines right after each one explodes, at least 15 s before the next zombie arrives, and keep one armed per row. They are best against footballs and pole vaulters.
Don't put producers (sun_shroom, sunflower) in a row with no fume_shroom. A leak kills them and wrecks the economy. Both sun_shrooms were lost in wave 10 to zombies that got past the fumes.
Pole vaulters jump the first plant, so a wall_nut doesn't stop them. Put a potato_mine or a second fume_shroom behind the nut.
Keep a sun reserve of 150+ for waves 8-10, and cherry_bomb a clump of coneheads or footballs before col 3. I again ended with 50 sun and an unused bomb, so don't hold it.
Check every row, row 0 included, each wave. Leaks start in rows with zero or one attacker, and once the mowers are spent one leak ends the level. All 4 remaining mowers fired in wave 10.

Waves 8-10 bring many coneheads and footballs together. Have 2+ fume_shrooms plus a wall_nut in every row by wave 6, and spend spare sun on that rather than on more economy.
Never leave a row empty of attackers. Rows 0 and 2 had 0 attackers by the end, so I should have rebuilt them before wave 10 arrived.
situation_lessons: Night: start with sun_shrooms in cols 0-1, then sunflowers. There is no falling sun, so income stops growing once you stop planting producers. Stop adding producers around wave 5.
Night: put the first fume_shroom in each row in col 2 or 3 before wave 3. It reaches 4 tiles, so it hits zombies chewing a nut in col 5-6.
Night: puff_shrooms cost 0 sun, so use them as sacrificial blockers in col 3. They gave only brief delays against coneheads and footballs, so don't rely on them for kills.
Night: potato_mines in col 4 were eaten or exploded in waves 2, 4, 6, 9 and 10. Replant them each time, and use the free mushroom slots before the sun-heavy waves.
Night: footballs appear from about wave 6 and again in wave 10. Pair a mine with a cherry_bomb in the football's row, and have 150 sun ready when the first one shows up.
Night: wave 10 is the biggest, and it hit rows 0, 2, 3 and 4 together. Before it, rebuild every dead fume_shroom and wall_nut and keep sun for emergency replants during the wave.
Night: use the mowers only as a last resort. Treat a spent mower as a failed row and rebuild its defense right away.
Night: build fume_shroom lines in rows 0 and 2 early. The grave-free cols 0-5 there are enough space for 2 fumes plus a nut.

history.summary: I won because the plan worked: sun_shrooms paid for 2-3 fume_shrooms in every row, with wall_nuts and puff_shroom blockers in front, so only one fume_shroom died before wave 20 and 5 mowers were left.

Row breaking: replant fumes and nuts at once and keep 150+ sun in reserve. Check every row each wave, row 0 included.
lessons: Fume_shrooms are the main killers. Put 2-3 per row in cols 2-4 and replace dead ones immediately. Holding them in every row, row 0 and row 4 included, won this level.
Build the economy first. Put sun_shrooms in cols 0-1 and add a few sunflowers before the first zombies arrive. Stop adding producers around wave 4-5 and put the sun into defense.

The biggest waves are around 8-10 and the last wave (20), with coneheads, screen doors and footballs together. Have 2+ fumes plus a nut in every row before them. Rebuild any dead fume or nut right after each wave.
Footballs are the late threat: in wave 20 one killed two wall_nuts in row 3 before it reached the fumes. Keep a mine armed in the football's row, or bomb it, rather than counting on nuts.

Night: put the first fume_shroom in each row in col 2 or 3 before wave 3, then add a second one. Rows with 3 attackers held easily. Fumes go through screen doors.
Night: use puff_shrooms as free col-3 blockers. They bought time for the fumes behind them, but they died in the last wave, so replant them.

Night: the usual pressure points are wave 9-10 and wave 20. Before them, rebuild all dead fumes and nuts and keep 150+ sun for emergency replants.
Night: the winning build was cols 2-4 fumes with a puff_shroom in col 3 and a nut in col 5. Row 4 was already limited by graves, so it could only hold 3 fumes and puffs.
Night: use the mowers only as a last resort. Treat a spent mower as a failed row and rebuild its defense right away. Losing none here shows the build was strong enough.
Night: wall_nuts at col 5-6 take the football hits. Replace damaged ones before the final wave and keep 2 free sun slots for emergency fume replants.

history.summary: Won because fume_shrooms in cols 1-3 of every row killed nearly everything, and free puff_shrooms plus mowers absorbed the late pressure, though row 3 broke at wave 5 (no wall_nut, no mower afterward) and the last wave left fumes damaged and sun low.

history.summary: Won by surviving to wave 20 on a conveyor level: the belt's free one-use cards (doom, ice, hypno) cleared the football and dancer clumps, and the fume_shrooms and scaredy_shrooms that the belt supplied held the front, but 3 mowers were left.
history.plan:
Economy: Start with 50 sun, so plant a sun_shroom or sunflower first in cols 0-1 of rows 1-3. Add producers until about wave 4, then put all sun into defense. If this is a conveyor level, use each card as it arrives and don't let the belt fill.
Layout: Graves block cols 4-9 in several rows, so defend in cols 0-5. Put 2-3 fume_shrooms per row in cols 1-3 (col 4 where it's open), with puff_shrooms as cheap blockers or fillers in col 3-4. Put wall_nuts in cols 4-5 in front of the fumes.
Zombies: Expect basic zombies and coneheads early, then pole vaulters, screen doors, footballs, dancers and flags in waves 8-10 and the final wave. Back up every nut with a second fume or an armed potato_mine in col 3-4, planted 15 s or more before the zombies arrive. Fire cherry_bomb on clumps before col 3.
Maintenance: Check every row between waves. Replace damaged nuts (under 50%) and dead fumes at once, including rows 0 and 4. Keep 150+ sun in reserve for waves 8-10 and the final wave. Don't put producers in a row without a fume_shroom.

The belt's cheap shooters (scaredy_shroom, puff_shroom, fume_shroom) died often, roughly 16 lost in total. Replace fumes in the row first, because scaredy_shrooms are weak blockers and die to footballs.
Row 1 and row 2 lost their mowers (waves 14 and 20), and rows 0-2 leaked the most. Give the open rows extra fumes and keep a hypno or doom in reserve for them.
Use grave_buster on graves in cols 4-5 only when nothing urgent needs the card. Free cells there give more room for fumes in front of the line.

history.summary: I lost because the two water rows (2 and 3) only had one or two lily-pad peashooters each, with no wall_nuts, repeaters or bombs. Coneheads and zombies chewed through them in waves 9-10 while I held unspent sun.
